feature: A long edit plays a minute without losing a frame, and the walk says so honestly
summary: The 6 minute reference edit already showed every frame while it played: the one dropped frame a minute the speed walk kept reporting was its counting. The walk now counts the frames the picture actually skipped and names where any lost frame was due.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The button on step 1 opens your own copy of the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev; once made, File > Open reaches it too (Cmd-Shift-G, ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev). The numbers come from Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh.

try.do: Open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below and park the playhead at 0:15.
Press Space and watch a minute of it, through the dissolves, the push and the cube.
Watch the first moment after Space: the picture starts moving about a twentieth of a second after the press.
Pause, pick a clip and press B to cut it while it plays: that is the edit cost still being worked on.

evaluate: Does a minute of play look perfectly even to you, with no hitch at the transitions?
Does the start after Space feel immediate?
Does a cut with B while playing still feel like it catches for a moment?
rough: Three one-minute plays, every look recorded: each new picture came 25 to 38 ms of edit time after the one before, never one skipped. The old count still read 1, 0 and 1 dropped, from the start's first tick and the last picture in flight. New count: 0, 0 and 0 of 1817; the speed walk afterwards also 0.
The first new picture after Space comes 50 to 67 ms after the press. It is now its own number in the walk, not a lost frame.

Still not reached on this task: an edit while playing holds the window 11 to 51 ms against the bar of 16 (blade 35, pick from nothing 51), and a dragged playhead's picture is 3 refreshes behind at worst against 1.
No mock covers this: it is a measurement and speed change with nothing new on screen.
